docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Flingdia is a declarative system for spatial reasoning. Its semantics are described in:

Olivier, F., Diéguez, M., and Schultz, C. (2026). Declarative Spatial Reasoning in Temporal Here-and-There with Constraints. In ASPOCP 2026: 19th Workshop on Answer Set Programming and Other Computing Paradigms, FLoC 2026, Lisbon, Portugal.

This documentation gives a brief overview of the language and its encodings.

docs.title: Geometric sorts
docs.text:
Flingdia programs use the standard clingo language extended with spatial atoms. Before using a spatial atom, declare each geometric object with one of the ordinary ASP predicates point/1, rect/1, or line/1. Declaring a sort determines the parameters available to an object.

point(a).
point(b).
rect(c).

Traditional pooling methods, like point(a;b)., can be used to facilitate the declaration. Each geometric sort corresponds to parameters as follows:

The geometric constraints applying to geometric sorts are encoded as validity axioms (see axioms).

docs.title: Spatial relations
docs.text:
Spatial relations are theory atoms of the form &relation(arguments). For example, the following declaration places a to the left of b:

&left(a,b).

Relation names are overloaded: the types of their arguments determine their meaning. Thus &left(a,c) also works, for instance, for point a and rectangle c. The geometric meaning of each relation is described on the relation page for its argument types. Check the meaning of &left(a,b) in the point-point relation page.

docs.title: Temporal operators
docs.text:
Temporal operators are theory atoms that locate a formula in time. The horizon is 0 by default (a static scene) and is set with -c n=…. For example, the following places a on the table in the initial state:

&on(a,table) :- &initial.

The operators &true, &initial, &next, &prev, &eventually, &always, &until, and &not are defined on the semantics page.

docs.title: Running Flingdia
docs.text:
Install metasp and matplotlib (pip install metasp matplotlib). Matplotlib is required for the default diagram printer.

Run Flingdia from this directory. For example:

metasp solve flingo --meta-config config.yaml \
    --warn=no-atom-undefined \
    --project=show \
    instances/TEMP/blocks_world.lp  0 \
    -c display_time=7  \
    -c n=5

The arguments mean:

  • The input file is followed by the number of models to compute (0 means all).
  • -c n=5 sets the temporal horizon.
  • --project=show projects solutions onto the displayed atoms.
  • -c display_time=7 keeps diagrams open for 7 seconds.
  • By default, Flingdia displays diagrams of the solutions. Add --printer table_printer to print only numeric tables, or --printer none to use the bare model output.

Each example file under instances/ begins with a block comment containing its complete launch command, which can be copied and run from this directory.

Default axioms: definedness and inertia

By default, Flingdia assigns values to every parameter of every declared object in the initial state. Parameter values then persist through time by inertia unless a rule or action supports a change.

Add the following facts to an input program to disable either default:

&partial.       % Allow parameters to remain undefined.
&not_inertia.   % Disable persistence of parameter values.

The directives are independent, so an input program may use either one or both. See the axioms page for the complete encoding.

docs.title: Time horizon
docs.text:
Default temporal horizon is 0, meaning that the scene is static. Override with -c n=….

#const n = 0.

docs.title: &true
docs.text: true(&true,I) :- formula(st,&true), time(I).

docs.title: &initial
docs.text:
true(&initial,0) :- formula(st,&initial).
:- formula(st,&initial), true(&initial,I), I!=0.

docs.title: &next
docs.text:
true(F,I+1) : time(I+1) :- formula(st,&next(F)), true(&next(F),I).
true(&next(F),I) :- formula(st,&next(F)), true(F,I+1), time(I).

docs.title: &prev
docs.text:
true(F,I-1) : time(I-1) :- formula(st,&prev(F)), true(&prev(F),I).
true(&prev(F),I) :- formula(st,&prev(F)), true(F,I-1), time(I).

docs.title: &eventually
docs.text:
true(F,J) : time(J), I<=J :- true(&eventually(F),I).
true(&eventually(F),I) :- formula(st,&eventually(F)), true(F,J), I<=J, time(I), time(J).

docs.title: &not
docs.text:
true(&not(F),I) :- formula(st,&not(F)), not true(F,I), time(I).
:- true(&not(F),I), true(F,I), time(I).

docs.title: &always
docs.text:
true(F,J) :- true(&always(F),I), time(J), I <= J.
true(&always(F),I) :- formula(st,&always(F)), time(I), true(F,J) : time(J), I <= J.

docs.title: &until
docs.text:
true(&until(F,G),I) :- formula(st,&until(F,G)), time(I), time(K), I <= K, true(G,K), true(F,J) : time(J), I <= J < K.
until_witness(F,G,I,K) : time(K), I <= K :- formula(st,&until(F,G)), true(&until(F,G),I), time(I).
true(G,K) :- until_witness(F,G,I,K).
true(F,J) :- until_witness(F,G,I,K), time(J), I <= J < K.

Without the rule below, G can be true before the G that is considered to satisfy the until condition. Indeed, we select an arbitrary future witness J, and not require G to be false before J. If we want that G must be false every time before J, add this constraint.

:- until_witness(F,G,I,K), true(G,J), time(J), I <= J < K.

It forbids choosing witness J whenever G was already true at some earlier I with K≤I<J. But standard until semantics does not require the earliest witness, so this constraint is optional and stronger than necessary. Standard encodings only require some witness J where G holds. Forcing the earliest such J is an additional minimization choice, not part of ordinary until semantics.

docs.title: Show
docs.text:
Project onto Boolean configurations (relations + ordinary atoms), not coordinate witnesses. Do not #show val/2 — that re-expands every &in assignment. show-time.lp only auto-shows formula(atom,…); spatial atoms need an explicit show.

#show true/1. #show val/2.

#show true(S,T) : true(S,T), formula(spatial,S).
#show true(S,T) : true(S,T), formula(atom,S).
#show invalid_relation_arg/1.
#show invalid_action_arg/1.

&show{}.
